hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM trained with lambdarank on user-groups capped at 6 consecutive rows, over base5 plus within-user duration features and out-of-fold item/author rates, will beat the 0.6016 baseline by a large margin.
rationale: Three mechanisms stack: (a) the loss becomes a ranking loss whose position discount is applied over ~6-item training lists that match the ~5.6-item lists actually scored, so gradient weight is spent where the metric is; (b) item_agg supplies out-of-fold video/author long-view propensities that vary across a user's rows and therefore actually reorder the list, which no identity embedding can do as cheaply; (c) dur_feats supplies within-user duration rank, and long_view is a duration-thresholded outcome, so duration is the most mechanically direct predictor available. Trees also handle these dense numeric signals far better than an FM over pure categoricals.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] says the loss is mismatched and [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists loss change first; published pairwise-vs-pointwise swaps on short lists typically move nDCG by 0.01-0.02. [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] only rules out STATIC fields, not outcome-aggregated ones, and item long-view rate is the single strongest within-user-varying signal available [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]; on KuaiRand-scale logs that is usually worth 0.03-0.05 alone. [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] is corrected by chunking to 6, worth a further small amount. Summing conservatively and discounting for overlap between item_agg and duration gives ~+0.06 over 0.6016, i.e. ~0.663, far above [SEED_NOISE] of 0.0008.

block_justifications.base5: video_id, author_id, tab and dur_bucket vary across a user's own rows so they can reorder the list, and 99.9% of valid videos are seen in train [HIGH_COVERAGE]; it is also the exact field set the 0.6016 baseline uses, keeping the comparison anchored.
block_justifications.dur_feats: long_view is a duration-thresholded outcome and the within-user duration percentile is by construction a within-user-varying quantity [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], which is the duration-bias direction the organizers list as unexplored [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold video/author long-view and click rates differ between the items shown to one user, so unlike a user-side term they can change that user's ordering, and they are the highest-signal non-static feature not covered by [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD].

hypothesis: Adding the cross_agg block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's own historical long-viewed duration) to the iteration-1 LightGBM lambdarank configuration will give the model the explicit personalised user-item interaction signal that the FM absorbs implicitly, and beat 0.60209.
rationale: The organizers state the user_id x video_id interaction absorbs most of the learnable signal, but a tree model cannot synthesise that interaction from raw high-cardinality IDs the way an FM dot product does. cross_agg hands the interaction to the trees pre-computed and, crucially, it varies across the items shown to one user, so unlike user_agg it can actually reorder that user's list. The duration-relative-to-user-history component is also the duration-bias direction the organizers flag as unexplored, expressed in a within-user-varying form.
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 added item-side quality and within-user duration and moved +0.0007 over the FM, i.e. those two families are almost fully redundant with what the FM already encodes as item bias. The one thing the FM has that iteration 1 lacked is the personalised interaction term the organizers name as carrying most of the signal [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD / their diagnosis], and cross_agg is the only block supplying it in a within-user-varying form [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. Since the FM gets 0.6016 largely from that term alone, adding it on top of item quality plus duration should compound rather than duplicate; I price that compounding at roughly 1-1.5% relative on a 0.60 base, so +0.009, an order of magnitude above [SEED_NOISE] of 0.0008.

hypothesis: Retraining the best configuration on only the last three training days (min_date=20220419) will beat 0.60209, because the evaluation window sits on the far side of an exposure-regime change and the oldest 80% of the log teaches a selection structure that no longer holds.
rationale: On 22 April ~80% of impressions were diverted to a randomised experiment, so which impressions reach the standard log, and their within-list composition, changed at the split boundary [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE]. A model fit on 14 days of the old regime spends most of its capacity on the residual structure of the pre-change logging policy. Truncating to the three days closest to the boundary is the only lever available that moves the training distribution toward the evaluation regime, and it simultaneously shortens each user's logged history so the per-user list length in training (~13 rows/user over 3 days) moves toward the ~5.6 of validation [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]. It is high variance because it discards ~80% of rows, which will make the out-of-fold item rates noisier; that trade is the experiment.
expected_gain_derivation: [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE] is the only documented structural difference between the two windows that is not a feature-engineering question, and it is untested. The CF observation [CF_DIAGNOSTIC_DIVERGENCE] shows the standard valid log is a selected surface whose within-list structure disagrees with true preference, which means regime-specific structure is worth several times [SEED_NOISE]. Iterations 1 and 2 moved the metric by 0.0007 and -0.0005 with feature changes, so feature space is near-flat at ~0.602; a distribution-matching change is the remaining axis with a plausible 0.01-scale effect. I take a mean of +0.006 with a wide two-sided spread (a -0.01 outcome from data loss is equally live).
